correctness.rationale: The proof fixes flux normalization, ring size, Hilbert-Schmidt norm and degenerate exceptional phases. Exact Fourier diagonalization yields a pairwise cosine-difference product; modular-sum/difference independence for odd cycles and parity coupling for even cycles establish the complete min-gap formulas. Monotone crossing gives unique even optimizers; odd midpoints give unique odd optimizers. Orthogonal Fourier matrix units diagonalize the time-averaged conjugation superoperator, giving both an upper bound and exact saturation at odd half-periods of a minimum-gap pair. All-size uniqueness is analytic. The standalone standard-library checker replayed 11,446 finite diagnostics, which are additional tests, not the proof.

value.rationale: The smallest Bohr frequency is the slowest phase-dephasing scale among all coherences in a finite isolated ring. Its reciprocal is exactly the sharp asymptotic Hilbert-Schmidt Cesaro channel-error envelope. Solving the all-size magnetic flux design problem yields a unique global two-phase classification with a substantial parity discontinuity (limiting optimum pi/2 versus pi/3) and sharp quadratic size scaling. This is a natural complete spectral-control invariant, not an arbitrary numeric slice or a restatement of generic average uniformity.
